title: Polling vs WebSockets: How Do Live Updates Work?
sources: websocket.org, 'The Road to WebSockets: From HTTP Polling to RFC 6455' (websocket.org/guides/road-to-websockets): with polling the client asks the server for updates at fixed intervals; most responses carry no new data, wasting bandwidth and server work; WebSocket (RFC 6455, 2011) keeps one persistent connection open

websocket.org, 'WebSocket vs HTTP' (websocket.org/comparisons/http): HTTP is request-response, the server cannot send unless asked; a WebSocket is a full-duplex connection where client and server can both send messages at any time; used for chat, live sports scores, multiplayer games, collaborative editing
Wikipedia, 'WebSocket': standardized by the IETF as RFC 6455 in 2011; provides a full-duplex communication channel over a single TCP connection, started with an HTTP Upgrade handshake
